steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media representations of crime: the media over-represent violent and sexual crime (12% actual but 60-70% media coverage). The media under-represent corporate and white-collar crime. This distortion creates a false public perception.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Moral panics (Cohen): a condition where the media defines a group as a threat to societal values. Cohen's mods and rockers study: media exaggerated minor beach fights, creating a moral panic that labelled them as 'folk devils'.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Deviancy amplification spiral: media exaggeration -> increased public concern -> increased policing -> more arrests -> more media coverage -> further exaggeration. The spiral makes the 'problem' appear bigger than it really is.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Fear of crime: media coverage increases fear, especially among vulnerable groups (elderly, women). However, those who fear crime most are least likely to be victims. Young men are the most likely victims but fear crime least.
